newsitem.title: USA: GE settles injury case for $5 million - lawyers.
newsitem.headline: GE settles injury case for $5 million - lawyers.

text.p: General Electric Co. has agreed to pay $5 million to settle a lawsuit brought by a man burned over 70 percent of his body after a GE circuit breaker exploded in 1995, plaintiffs' lawyers said Thursday.
The suit was brought by Juan Vega, an electrician who worked installing a GE electrical system at a Haggar men's wear factory in Dallas, the lawyers said in a statement.
On July 1, 1995, after testing the equipment, the circuit breaker exploded, engulfing the worker in flames, molten plastic and metal, the lawyers said.
Vega, who was 29 at the time of the accident, was rushed to the hospital where he underwent several skin grafts and additional surgery.
He has since returned to work, a spokeswoman for the lawyers said.
Reached at his home, GE spokesman Bruce Bunch said he was not aware of the suit.
